content: 1. Bremelanotide may slow gastric emptying, which can reduce the absorption rate and extent of oral medications taken concurrently. Avoid using it with oral drugs that require specific threshold concentrations for efficacy. 2. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of brigatinib by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. Strong CYP3A4 inducers may reduce brigatinib efficacy. 3. Buprenorphine (subdermal implant, transdermal, or long-acting injection) and phenobarbital both increase sedation. Use alternative treatments if possible, and limit use to patients without adequate alternative options. 4. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of cabozantinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. If unavoidable, increase the cabozantinib dose (40 mg/day for Cometriq or 20 mg/day for Cabometyx) and resume the previous dose 2–3 days after discontinuing the inducer. 5. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of capivasertib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A inducers, as they reduce capivasertib exposure and efficacy. 6. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of capmatinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 7. Phenobarbital decreases ceritinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 8. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of cobicistat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration is necessary, monitor for virologic response loss. 9. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of copanlisib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. 10. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of dabigatran by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration, as P-gp inducers reduce dabigatran systemic exposure. 11. Phenobarbital decreases dabrafenib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 12. Phenobarbital reduces the effects of dalteparin by increasing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 13. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of dantrolene by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 14. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of daridorexant by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 15. Phenobarbital increases the levels or effects of darolutamide. Avoid coadministration with combined P-gp and strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers. 16. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of deflazacort by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inducers. 17. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of dexlansoprazole by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 18. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of dihydroergotamine (including intranasal formulations) by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 19. Phenobarbital reduces dolutegravir levels by increasing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration due to insufficient data for dosage adjustment. 20. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of dronedarone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 21. Phenobarbital reduces duloxetine levels by inducing CYP1A2 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 22. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of duvelisib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A inducers, as they reduce duvelisib exposure and efficacy. 23. Phenobarbital reduces edoxaban levels by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration with potent P-gp inducers. 24. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of elacestrant by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 25. Phenobarbital reduces eliglustat levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A inducers, as they significantly decrease eliglustat exposure. 26. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of elvitegravir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with CYP3A inducers, as this may lead to reduced plasma concentrations and therapeutic failure. 27. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of encorafenib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 28. Phenobarbital decreases the effects of enoxaparin by increasing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 29. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of entrectinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 30. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of enzalutamide by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 31. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of erdafitinib by altering its metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP2C9 or CYP3A4 inducers. 32. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of ergotamine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 33. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of erythromycin (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, or stearate) by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 34. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of esomeprazole by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 35. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of eszopiclone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 36. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced; use nonhormonal contraceptives instead. 37. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of everolimus by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Coadministration is contraindicated. 38. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of fedratinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 39. Phenobarbital and fentanyl (including intranasal, transdermal, iontophoretic, and transmucosal formulations) both increase sedation. Limit use to patients without adequate alternative options, and monitor closely for respiratory depression and sedation. 40. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of fexinidazole by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 41. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of finerenone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 42. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of flurazepam by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 43. Phenobarbital decreases the effects of fondaparinux by increasing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 44. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of fostamatinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 45. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of fruquintinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 46. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of ganaxolone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inducers. If unavoidable, consider increasing the ganaxolone dose without exceeding the maximum daily dose. 47. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of gilteritinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with combined P-gp and strong CYP3A inducers. 48. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of glasdegib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A inducers. 49. Phenobarbital decreases the effects of heparin by increasing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 50. Phenobarbital and hydrocodone increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy, potentially causing profound sedation, respiratory depression, coma, or death. Limit dosages and monitor closely for respiratory depression and sedation. 51. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of ibrutinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A inducers, as they decrease ibrutinib plasma concentrations by approximately 10-fold. 52. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of idelalisib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers, as they significantly reduce idelalisib systemic exposure. 53. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of infigratinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 54. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of irinotecan (including liposomal formulations) by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 55. Phenobarbital and isocarboxazid should not be coadministered due to central nervous system depressant effects. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 56. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of isosorbide dinitrate and mononitrate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 57. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of istradefylline by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. 58. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of ivabradine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with moderate CYP3A4 inducers. 59. Phenobarbital decreases ivacaftor levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers, as systemic exposure is substantially reduced (~9-fold). 60. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of ivosidenib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers, as they decrease ivosidenib plasma concentrations. 61. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of ixazomib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A inducers, as they significantly reduce ixazomib Cmax and AUC. 62. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of larotrectinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers.
